nodes.label: The wrapper had no branch for combined short-flag clusters, so grep -rn silently fell through to the catch-all delegate
nodes.norm_label: the wrapper had no branch for combined short-flag clusters, so grep -rn silently fell through to the catch-all delegate
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L2527] "`-rn` is a *combined* short flag. The `case` matches `-r` and `-n` separately but has no branch for `-rn`, so it falls into the catch-all `-*) delegate`." L3681 records the effect and the fix together: combined flags `-rn`, `-in`, `-rni` meant "**`grep -rn pat .` silently used GNU grep**", repaired by splitting clusters of verified-safe characters and still delegating anything containing value-taking (`A B C m e`) or ambiguous (`P z E u`) flags.

nodes.label: In tgrep -E means --encoding, so passing grep's -E through killed the search
nodes.norm_label: in tgrep -e means --encoding, so passing grep's -e through killed the search
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L3682] "In tgrep `-E` means `--encoding`, not extended-regexp → `grep -E -r pat .` died with `unsupported encoding: pat`, exit 2". The fix is to drop `-E` entirely rather than translate it, because tgrep's default regex is already ERE-like. This is a same-letter different-meaning collision, so a flag name that agrees between the two tools is not evidence that the flag means the same thing.

nodes.label: BRE-dialect patterns reach tgrep and return zero matches silently, which reads as 'not found'
nodes.norm_label: bre-dialect patterns reach tgrep and return zero matches silently, which reads as 'not found'
nodes.rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L4470] "Wrapper hanya memeriksa **flag**, tidak memeriksa **sintaks pola**. tgrep pakai Rust regex (ERE-like), sedangkan `grep` tanpa `-E` itu BRE". Measured per case at L4474-L4476 — `foo\|bar`, `foo\+` and `a\{2,3\}` each gave **kosong** with exit 1 — and L4479 states the consequence: "Exit 1 + tanpa output itu identik dengan \"tidak ditemukan\". Jadi `grep -rn 'TODO\|FIXME' .` akan melapor **tidak ada yang cocok**, padahal ada." The fix is a guard on pattern syntax, not on flags; delegating is correct for those patterns.

The same behaviour is recorded as deliberate rather than as a defect at L6358: "hasil **tidak** akan selalu sama dengan GNU grep di repo git, karena tgrep menghormati `.gitignore` (nggak masuk `node_modules/`, `dist/`) sedangkan GNU grep menelusuri semuanya. Itu perilaku yang benar". So an indexed and an unindexed run are not comparable on match count, and the index was moved aside to a dated backup.

That matters because `cmd | grep foo` is a common pattern." This is the reason stdin stays delegated to GNU grep rather than approximated, and L3698 preserves the path as "`grep pat` → still GNU grep (tgrep has no stdin; `-` isn't supported)".

nodes.label: sd is not a drop-in sed: it rewrites files in place by default
nodes.norm_label: sd is not a drop-in sed: it rewrites files in place by default
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04214] "A transparent `sed` → `sd` wrapper would silently turn every read-only command you type into a destructive file rewrite. `grep` → tgrep got away with a wrapper because search is side-effect-free; substitution is not." The three supporting rows were re-measured rather than assumed — L4194 "file went `a a a` → `X X X`", L4195 "`sed 's/a/X/'` → `X a a` vs `sd a X` → `X X X`. No flag reconciles these" — and L4196 records that sed's script commands (`2d`, `2q`, `y/ab/ba/`, `2i\`, `1!d`) have no sd equivalent at all.

nodes.label: A PATH shim for sed would be inherited by build systems, which call sed with -n, p and \1
nodes.norm_label: a path shim for sed would be inherited by build systems, which call sed with -n, p and \1
rationale: [05 - Conversations/home-belajarcarabelajar/2026-09-28 - set-tgrep-as-default-search-command [ses_f16aafeacffe6TkaP4jl5u2iDd].md:L04218] "I gave `grep` a **PATH shim** at `~/.local/bin/grep`, which every process inherits — build scripts included. That was safe only because the wrapper delegates anything risky back to GNU grep. For `sed` that same approach would be destructive, and this machine would actually hit it". L4210 names the callers and the disqualifiers: `sed -n '2,25p' "$0"` in an installer self-extracting header, `sed -nE 's/.../\1/p' package.json` and `sed 's/\r$//' .env` in `scripts/deploy/*.sh`, `scripts/ops/provision-vps.sh` and `distribution/snipset-cli/install.sh`, plus CMake's own modules — "`-n`, `p`, and `\1` alone rule it out", so sed stays reachable as `/usr/bin/sed` and is only reached interactively through `alias ssd='sd -p'`.
